summary: Small estate affidavit for collection of personal property.
applies: Title 18-C (Maine Uniform Probate Code), effective 2019-09-01 — see transition_18a.

governing.title: Collection of personal property by affidavit
governing.why: Collection of personal property by affidavit (small estate, $40,000 limit, 30 days after death).

governing.title: Effect of affidavit
governing.why: Effect of the affidavit; protection of the person paying/delivering.

considerations.title: Collection of personal property by affidavit
considerations.note: At least 30 days must have elapsed since death before using the affidavit.

considerations.title: Collection of personal property by affidavit
considerations.note: The affiant must be a successor entitled to the property.

transition_18a: Eligibility turns on the current §3-1201 threshold ($40,000, inflation-adjusted) and the 30-day wait — both raised/changed from former 18-A. Title 18-C applies to estates of decedents who die on or after 2019-09-01, and to any proceeding pending on or commenced after that date. For a decedent who died before 2019-09-01, former Title 18-A supplies the substantive succession rules even though the proceeding itself runs under 18-C. See _index/18a-key-diffs.json (governing rule: 18-C §8-301).
